1. During the course of hearing, it emerges that no quota is prescribed in the cadre of Designated Officers, Class-I, in the General State Service in the Commissionerate of Food and Drugs Control Administration Recruitment Rules, 2013, for two source of recruitment.

sentences.text: 2. In the affidavit-in-reply filed by the Respondent No.1-State dated 07.12.2015 also this has been admitted.

Paragraphs-5 and 6, thereof, reads thus;
"5.

It is submitted that as per the provision of section 36 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, it is mandatory to have a Designated Officer for each District to complete the process of enforcement of the Act.

However, the Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011, which came into effect on 05th August, 2011, the State Government created the post of Designated Officers as mentioned in detail hereafter.

There are total 27 posts of Designated Officers, Class-I, out of which 23 posts are advertised with intention of filling by direct selection through Gujarat Public Service Satishkumar Ashabhai Patel S/O ... vs State Of Gujarat & on 2 December, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139972649/
1 Commission.

sentences.text: These posts were created by parts, over a period between the year 2013-14 and 1015-16.
In the fist instance 20 posts in 2012-13, 5 posts during the year 2013-14 by the orders dated 24-05-2012 and 17-06- 2013.
These posts were created keeping in view total 25 Districts at the time.
Moreover 2 additional post of Designated Officers were created during the year 2015-16 keeping in view the new Districts created.

Thus, as on today 23 vacancies are advertised with intention of filling through direct selection process and 4 posts are kept reserved for filling them by way of promotion process, against total 27 available posts of Designated Officers.
These 4 posts kept vacant for promotion are as per the availability of candidates till 2020.
6. It is further submitted that the procedure for filling all these 27 posts could not be initiated immediately as the recruitment rules were finally published only after 29 th August, 2013.

It is admitted that there HC-NIC Page 2 of 4 Created On Sat Jul 22 00:34:00 IST 2017 is no fix ratio for Direct appointment and Promotion in the Recruitment Rules, however, this does not restrict filling of posts by way of promotion as it specifically to facilitate filling of these posts immediately either by promotion or by direct selection.
It can be said that the provision is accommodative and not of restrictive in nature.

This provision was specifically included to accommodate filling the post of Designated Officer as it is the important missing link in the hierarchy of Food Safety Officers, implementing the various provisions of the act and rules. "
3.

This Court also notices that there is availability of four officers in the Feeder Cadre, as per the say of the State, but, 23 posts have been advertised and GPSC has been requested by the State by sending a request for filling-up the posts in question.

4. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of 'ORISSA JUDICIAL SERVICES. VS. STATE OF ORISSA AND OTHERS', AIR 1991 SC 382, having realized that there was absence of any quota for two source of recruitment, had directed thus:
"6.

entities.text: ORISSA JUDICIAL SERVICES. VS. STATE OF ORISSA AND OTHERS', AIR 1991 SC 382
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: While it is true that statutory rules can be supplemented by administrative instructions and the State Government in consultation HC-NIC Page 3 of 4 Created On Sat Jul 22 00:34:00 IST 2017 with the High Court is competent to prescribe quota for the two sources of recruitment to the service by administrative orders but it would be desirable and proper to prescribe the quota for recruitment to the Service in the rules themselves.
Absence of statutory provision in the Rules fixing the quota for the two sources of recruitment, results into a state of uncertainty leading to suspicion and litigation.
We are, therefore, of the opinion that the State Government should take immediate steps in consultation with the High Court for amending the Rules by prescribing the quota to remove the uncertainty.

If the statutory rules prescribe quota fixed for the two sources of recruitment, it would eliminate the exercise which the State Government and the High Court have to undergo every time whenever a vacancy arises for determining the question whether it should be filled up from which Satishkumar Ashabhai Patel S/O ... vs State Of Gujarat & on 2 December, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139972649/
2 of the two sources.
